summary: What Nora held in a room is now recoverable for a moment that has already passed. Her per-room position used to be overwritten on every fold with nothing behind it; it now keeps a history, which was the last missing piece — the transcript, the notebook and the culture account were already recoverable — so a room and an instant can be reconstructed into the state she was actually in then.
details: `standing` is one row per room, revised in place on every fold. The value it replaced was not stale, it was gone: nothing anywhere held it. A new `standing_revision` table records what the position was set to each time it moved, appended in the same transaction as the fold's own write, so a fold that is refused advances neither and a position that moved without being recorded is not a state the store can produce. The note and culture tiers already worked this way; this was the one model-written tier that did not.

Nothing about the existing read or write changed. The upsert is the same statement with the same values, every current caller behaves identically, and the head keeps its meaning — the history sits beside it.

A new read answers «what was the position here, then»: the newest revision at or before the instant asked about. The boundary is inclusive, because the timestamp is when the position was taken. A room with no fold before that instant answers «nothing», which is the same answer a room that has never been folded gives.

A point-in-time reader composes the four tiers into one reconstruction — the messages said by then, the position held then, the culture account current then, and the notebook as it stood then with each entry's body as it read then rather than as it reads now. It writes nothing, and that is checked rather than claimed: every table's row count is taken before and after.

The room's culture key and its notes' unit are required arguments and are not guessed. Both come from policy.toml rather than from the database, and a wrong key matches no rows, raises nothing and reads exactly like a room that had neither — the silent failure the culture tier's own migration spends a paragraph warning about.
limitations: No backfill. A room's history starts at its next fold, so any instant before this ships answers «no position» for every room, including rooms that have one today. Inserting the current head as a first revision would have attached a real timestamp to a provenance claim nothing observed, and a history whose earliest entries were manufactured is one a reader cannot tell apart from a recorded one.

Four columns on a note — its current head, its strike count, its next revisit and its last wake — are TODAY's values, not the instant's, because the note row itself has no history table. Everything a reader reconstructs from is honest: the body is the revision that stood then, returned beside the note so nobody resolves the head and quietly gets the current one; the fields that decide what the notebook showed — title, description, uncertainty, closing condition, anchor — really are written once at creation and never changed; and a note retired after the instant comes back reporting no retirement at all, because at that instant it had none. A first cut kept such a note in the notebook but handed it back carrying the time and the reason of a retirement that had not happened yet.

A reconstructed transcript shows media as the bare handle stored on the row, not as a description of what the photo or the voice note actually was. The live turn sees the description; the reconstruction reads the message table directly, one layer below where that join lives, so a room whose conversation turned on a picture reconstructs thinner than it happened. Closing it means building the reconstruction's transcript a layer up rather than reaching the join downwards.

Honcho-backed state — the peer card, the representation, anything the dialectic answers — is not in the reconstruction and cannot be. It is live and mutable by design with no chain to read backwards; returning today's copy beside a year-old transcript would be worse than returning none.

The tie-break among revisions sharing one instant is `fold_count`, not arrival order, because `fold_count` is what the row actually carries — but it is not strictly monotonic: a rebuild resets it to 1 (`debrief.py`) and a rollup fold carries the prior value forward unchanged (`standing_event.py`). Two revisions of the same room can share both `updated_at` and `fold_count`, and between those the pick is still arbitrary. Measured: not the common case, and never wrong about WHICH position was held, only about which of two identically-labelled ones the read returns.
Nothing reads this yet from an eval corpus or the CLI. The capability and its reader exist and are tested against real seeded rows; wiring a case to a real past moment is separate work.
